finding.what: The terrain does not carry '15 times': each mesa is a ridge 25 rows deep, and at the landing its top surface projects as height, so Ireland reads about 2-3x its neighbours and the 1.5 % World mesa about a quarter of Ireland.
finding.why: Halving the depth of a cell (cells and values unchanged, a view choice) removes most of the depth term, so screen height follows the value; check round 2 that Ireland now towers over World.

finding.what: The tilt lands at 22 deg, above the brief's own landing rule (elevation view, el <= 20, P10); from that height the receding tops still inflate the low mesas.
finding.why: A flatter landing reads heights, not footprints; one camera knob, check round 2 that Ireland does not hide the Netherlands behind it.

finding.what: With the depth term removed the whole terrain would shrink; the height scale is the lever that keeps the true ratio large on screen.
finding.why: Height of the value 25 from 110 to 150 (scale still fixed, vmin 0, vmax 25): Ireland keeps about its present screen size while World stays a sliver; check round 2 the Ireland top stays clear of the 7,663 GWh readout.

finding.what: The swing to the US column rises from the tilt's elevation to 18 deg while 176 TWh and 4.4 % land, changing two camera axes under new numbers.
finding.why: Holding the landing elevation makes the swing an azimuth-only drift (one change at a time, T5) and keeps the elevation view through MONDAY.
